checks: Least-active independence applies to the finite homogeneous row objectives. Four active rows are independent. If a full row had a full-cut minimum, at least three saturated columns would force the other three active rows into at most one coordinate direction, violating independence.

The centroid lemma's nonunit hypothesis follows once full-cut minima are ruled out. The capacity of a full row is positive because it is at least its least entry. Evaluating the ratio at its largest entry gives a full cut of value at most one, and the absence of a full-cut minimum makes the capacity strictly below that value. This row's capacity therefore lies in (0,1), which rules out every standard unit capacity vector even when this is the only full row.

The actual common centroid has positive coordinates, so the weighted gradient of each full row is strictly positive. Transferring a small amount of a positive entry from a row with at least two zeros to a full row leaves the donor's support and its zero capacity fixed. The receiving row then has strictly positive first-order gain. Thus any other active nonfull row has exactly one zero. At its hole h the multiplier estimate gives b_j≤1/3 for all j≠h.

For each active row t_i=b·X_i>0. It is the actual threshold for full rows. In any column h, Σ_i(t_i−X_ih)=b·1−1=0. With J={j:b_j>1/3} empty, every strict captured pair is central. With J={h} and one or more one-zero rows, they all have hole h and contribute strictly positive t_i, forcing a strictly negative full-row margin. This argument does not require the holes to be distinct.

With J={h} and all rows full, the accepted same-side lemma rules out zero margin at h since a boundary centroid coordinate equals 1/3. Zero sum forces a negative margin at h. If |J|≥2, the one-zero bound forces all rows to be full. In each proper section every index in J has the same strict margin sign. At a fixed h∈J some row has a negative margin by balance, so it strictly excludes every index in J.

In all cases a full row captures at least two vertices with coordinates at most 1/3. The accepted Schur theorem covers proper minimizing sections with zero margins and yields local C². The corrected central-pair lemma gives strictly positive optimized Hessian value after normalization. Degree-one homogeneity scales that Hessian by the positive reciprocal threshold, and a positive weight preserves the sign. The joint index bound would require 4+1≤4.
